fatal_errors: The proposed composition-series intervention does not reconstruct the temperature-dependent annealing and water-quenching study on fixed Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The assumed single-phase FCC as-cast baseline conflicts with the target alloy and its 1100 °C quenched baseline.

The proposed FCC-to-BCC martensitic transformation is fundamentally different from the reported BCC miscibility-gap spinodal decomposition, reciprocal chemical partitioning, and subsequent Ni-Al B2 ordering.
The hypothesis omits the hierarchical reciprocal BCC/B2 microstructure, minor FCC morphology, and hardness increase with quench temperature.

The cited evidence does not establish an Al-driven martensitic FCC-to-BCC mechanism in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni; it is largely about other alloy systems, configurational trends, FCC toughness, or FCC/HCP stability.
Atom-probe tomography does not directly measure electronic bonding or lattice distortion, so part of the proposed mechanistic test is not operationally valid.
explanation: The response addresses phase stability and offers a nominally controlled Al-content series with a falsification rule, but it does not recover the material, intervention, thermal conditions, baseline, mechanism, or principal outcome of the hidden study. Its only limited agreement is the generic expectation that Al can favor BCC-related structures. The experiment could test a separate composition-dependent hypothesis, but simultaneous thermal, cryogenic, corrosive, and radiation exposures would introduce confounding, and the proposed evidence does not support the claimed lattice-distortion-mediated martensitic mechanism. Thus it is neither an exact nor a well-supported plausible alternative.
